infra-oncall: noticing a sustained throughput drop on cluster-west since ~03:10 UTC. multiple workers restarted with OOMs, CPU sched looks normal, GPU mem churn high. rolling wave across pool-3 :fire:
maya: can you paste the worker logs and the kernel-selection traces?
samir: quick snapshot from worker-12 at 03:14:
```
[2026-03-18T03:14:02Z] ERROR worker-12 inference-serving: cudaMemcpy failed: out of memory
[2026-03-18T03:14:02Z] WARN kernel-router: selected fast_attn_int8 -> fallback generic_attention (switch_count=7 in last 2m)
[2026-03-18T03:14:02Z] INFO kvcache: evict_rate=928/s free=12MB active_hot=3
```
junaid: that fallback loop + high evict rate smells like fragmentation + small-batch churn. We rolled batch_adapt_v2 to 50% ~03:00 UTC.
maya: batch_adapt_v2 reduces target batch latency to favor low-latency small batches — more tiny batches => less contiguous allocations and more KV evicts. Can we confirm batch size distribution?
samir: profiler summary (worker-12, 03:10-03:20):
```
requests: 5.2k
avg batch size: 1.8
prev avg: 6.4
kernel_switches_per_request: 0.9 -> 2.7
mem_alloc_pattern: many small allocs, slab_util 23% -> fragmentation
```
maya: kernel_switches_per_request up -> increases transient allocations (fallback paths allocate temp buffers). Combined with KV evicts the allocator loses large free spans.
tess: copying telemetry: nv_alloc_hot_pages shows spike 03:11-03:16, sweep/slow-sweep count increased. Suggest mitigation: pin kernel routing to stable_fastpath for 1 hour and rollback batch_adapt_v2 rollout.
junaid: oncall actions: draining 2 noisy nodes in pool-3, kick off canary rollback for batch_adapt_v2, increase kvcache capacity by 25% for pool-3 ephemeral config.
infra-oncall: doing drain now, ETA 12m. also enabling per-worker allocation sampling for next 5m (`/admin/alloc-sample --duration 300 --level brief`).
deploy-bot: rollback started: batch_adapt_v2 -> 20% (canary) by tess at 03:22 UTC.
maya: follow-up checks: 1) confirm kernel pin prevents fast->fallback churn (add metric kernel_switch_rate) 2) check kvcache eviction backlog and set prefetch threshold +2 3) run allocator profile (`/tools/alloc-prof --workers pool-3 --out /tmp/alloc-03-18`)
samir: ran alloc-prof on worker-12, snippet:
```
slab-32MB: free_chunks=2 total_chunks=8
slab-8MB: free_chunks=1 total_chunks=16
largest_free_span=6MB (fragmented into 512k blocks)
```
maya: that largest_free_span < typical model KV chunk -> fragmentation causes extra allocations -> OOM.
tess: I'll schedule immediate config push: pin kernel routing to `stable_fastpath_v3` for pool-3 and bump kvcache by 25%. Also revert batch_adapt_v2 to previous thresholds.
junaid: good. after config push, let's re-evaluate after 10m and watch worker restarts/oom counts.
infra-oncall: config push applied at 03:28 UTC. starting metrics watch.
deploy-bot: config change: pin_kernel=stable_fastpath_v3 applied to pool-3 by tess at 03:28 UTC.
maya: initial signs look positive: kernel_switch_rate dropping, avg batch size creeping back up.
samir: worker restarts dropped to 0 in last 5m on affected nodes, evict_rate down to 140/s.
junaid: keep kvcache headroom and follow up with allocator sweep tuning in next patch. Need a postmortem with timeline and a perf regression test to catch this interaction.
maya: filing follow-up task and eval: add integration test that simulates small-batch churn + KV pressure so batch_adapt rollouts don't regress allocator behavior.
tess: noted, will coordinate patch and rollout guardrails. :thumbsup:
infra-oncall: closing alert state, will keep pager suppressed for 1h while we monitor. thanks all.
